newsitem.title: USA: U.S. rig count down 28 to 885 in latest survey.
newsitem.headline: U.S. rig count down 28 to 885 in latest survey.

text.p: The number of rigs exploring for oil and natural gas in the United States stood at 885 as of Friday, down 28 from the prior week and 138 above the year-ago total of 747, Baker Hughes Inc. reported.
The number of rigs drilling on land fell by 28 to 732, while rigs working offshore dipped by one to 125.
The number of rigs active in inland waters rose by one to 28. Among the individual states, the biggest changes occurred in Texas, which fell by 11, and Oklahamo, which fell by eight.
Rigs in the Gulf of Mexico fell by one to 120.
A total of 372 rigs were exploring for crude oil, up one from last week. The number of rigs searching for gas fell by 30 to 511, while the number of miscellaneous drilling projects rose one to two.
In Canada, the number of working rigs fell by three to 201, vs. 64 a year ago.
The weekly rig count reflects the number of rigs exploring for oil and gas, not those producing oil and gas.
There were 166 rigs under contract in the U.S. Gulf as of Friday, unchanged from a week ago, Offshore Data Services said.
The utilization rate for rigs working in the Gulf, based on a total fleet of 179, remained 92.7 percent.
The number of working rigs in the European/Mediterranean area remained unchanged at 103 rigs under contract out of a total fleet of 104, a utilization rate of 99.0 percent.
The worldwide rig count was unchanged at 573 out of a total fleet of 604, with an unchanged utilization rate 94.9 percent.
